A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RoboSpatial research work. All 18 pages of v1 and 19 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable, and corresponding methods, experiments, tables, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C report original VLM fine-tuning, generalization, data-scaling, reference-frame, and real-robot experimental results.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original benchmark and robot experiments, including newly reported general-knowledge evaluations and a grounding-data ablation.

M1.justification: The reported compatibility-generation rule changes from a threshold of 1% of the object's longest width or length in v1 Appendix A.2 to placement with at least 10 cm clearance along every axis in v2 Section 3.2.2 and Appendix B.4. The overall generation and fine-tuning approach remains; expanded projection and visibility-filtering descriptions do not independently establish further procedural changes.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on SpatialBench's position category from SpatialBot and on MMMU, MME, and MMBench. This substantially expands coverage to general multimodal knowledge and reasoning alongside spatial evaluation. The five source datasets, RoboSpatial-Home, BLINK, and robot tasks remain.

E2.justification: The main quantitative comparator set remains unchanged. However, v2 Figure 7 narrows the corresponding qualitative comparisons from v1 Figures 7–8 by omitting VILA, SpaceLLaVA, and the 3D models where previously shown, while adding untuned LLaVA-NeXT point predictions.

E3.justification: v1's separate training/validation/test splits become reallocated training/validation splits in v2, with main evaluation labeled RoboSpatial-Val. Validation-based checkpoint selection remains, without clarification of a separate final test. The stated evaluation total changes from 3,000 to 6,000 questions, and Home from 150 to 350. Table 11 adds grounding-only and spatial-only controls. These are reported protocol changes; unchanged main scores do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix D.3 and Table 10 add an analysis of whether spatial fine-tuning preserves general knowledge. Appendix D.4 and Table 11 isolate the contributions of grounding and spatial supervision. These address substantial new questions about retention and attribution; the existing scaling, reference-frame, transfer, and robot-failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Results continue to be presented as point estimates, including the newly added evaluations.

E6.justification: Home results are replaced under its revised reported size: fine-tuned RoboPoint's context score changes from 54.0 to 21.3 and compatibility from 48.0 to 88.6, so these are not established same-setting gains or losses. v2 adds SpatialBench scores, general-benchmark results, and ablation scores of 30.3/32.4/51.8/60.5 for base/grounding/spatial/both. Main, BLINK aggregate, robot, scaling, and per-frame scores remain unchanged. The retained couch/suitcase example changes GPT-4o from correct to incorrect.

T1.justification: The dataset and spatial-relation tuples retain their mathematical content. Neither version contains theorems or proofs; v2's expanded geometric explanations introduce no substantive formal derivation or theoretical result.

C1.justification: The central dataset, spatial-learning, and robotic-transfer contributions remain. The introduction narrows the 3D comparison claim: v1 says the results reinforce benefits of 3D-based training, whereas v2 explicitly calls the comparison inconclusive because pretraining data and base language models differ.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning containment, the top-down representation, and lack of joint robot-trajectory training, plus a rationale for excluding counting. It also interprets grounding supervision as complementary and spatial fine-tuning as preserving broader knowledge. The blanket retention statement overstates Table 10, where MME cognition decreases from 305.4 to 293.2; v1's human-centric-perspective failure qualification is omitted.

D1.justification: v2 substantially expands generation details, including camera transformations, projection, raycasting visibility checks, GPT-4o support-surface selection, and the 100k auxiliary grounding pairs. The grounding component already existed in v1. v2 also supplies a project link and states that data and generation code are publicly available, replacing v1's planned release. Model checkpoints, hardware, and principal training budgets are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work add AR/egocentric references such as Ego4D and AlanaVLM, localization-based spatial reasoning, and general evaluation benchmarks. Some planning/grasping citations and the criticism of LLM-generated annotations are removed. The central positioning as a robotics-specific spatial dataset remains.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting spans the abstract, introduction, method exposition, and experimental discussion. The generation explanation now separates 3D relationship extraction from 2D sampling, terminology is standardized, and the appendices are reorganized around limitations, dataset details, implementation, and results, with robot setup and qualitative discussion relocated.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 are redesigned, including a substantial rearrangement of Figure 3's comparison grid. v1 Figures 7–8 are merged into v2 Figure 7 with standardized image/result panels. The taxonomy table is removed while its content remains in prose; the out-of-domain table gains a SpatialBench column, Tables 10–11 are added, and several existing displays are relocated or restructured.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility and interpretability through fuller generation details, clearer limitations, and an ablation that separates spatial supervision from grounding. Additional evaluations broaden the evidence. The net gain is limited by unresolved links between revised evaluation settings and unchanged main scores, and by new overstatements: Table 10 does not support preservation across every benchmark, while Table 11 contradicts the main text's assertion that auxiliary grounding does not contribute to spatial performance.
